sentences.text: Corynebacterium striatum is part of the normal microbiota of human skin and nasal mucosa, and was long regarded as a cutaneous saprophyte.
It has been increasingly reported as the agent of community-acquired and nosocomial disease, helped by easier and more accurate identification from clinical cultures.
Biofilm formation on abiotic surfaces contributes to the persistence of virulent strains and to the spread of antimicrobial resistance in the hospital environment.
Multidrug-resistant strains have been associated with nosocomial outbreaks; one hospital investigation found a cluster in lower respiratory specimens from intensive care patients.
Reported infections have mostly involved the respiratory tract and the bloodstream, and reviews describe invasive infections in immunosuppressed and immunocompetent patients.
